parts.text: Which claim correctly states what regrouping or reordering does to the product?

options.text: Call the answer the product alone, with no check that the factors stay the same integers.
$(-2) \times \bigl((-3) \times 4\bigr)$ and $\bigl((-2) \times (-3)\bigr) \times 4$ both equal $24$, and any order of these factors keeps that product.
Treat the product as unchanged even when the factors are no longer these integers.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: Integer multiplication is associative and commutative, so regrouping or reordering these factors keeps the product $24$.

teacher.key_rationale: Associativity and commutativity keep the product of these integers the same under regrouping. Naming "product" alone substitutes a label. Dropping the integer-factor condition omits when the property applies.
